userStories.title: Add direct TabBar unit test for the `suspended` prop contract
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a direct TabBar unit test that pins the `suspended` prop's Left/Right navigation contract so that the presentational behavior is verified independently of its single ConfigScreen caller and cannot silently regress.
acceptanceCriteria: A new test in test/ui/tab-bar.test.tsx renders TabBar directly (not via ConfigScreen) with suspended={false} and asserts a Left or Right arrow key event fires tab navigation (the active chip changes / onChange is invoked). [oracle: bun test test/ui/tab-bar.test.tsx]

The same test file asserts that with suspended={true}, Left and Right arrow key events are suppressed and do NOT change the active tab / do NOT invoke navigation. [oracle: bun test test/ui/tab-bar.test.tsx]
The new test(s) reference the `suspended` prop by name so the presentational contract is explicitly pinned. [oracle: grep -q 'suspended' test/ui/tab-bar.test.tsx]
The test follows the established ink-testing-library render() + stdin.write style already used in the suite; no new test harness is introduced. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
TabBar source is unchanged unless a genuine test-seam gap forces it (test-only change). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
Verify the TabBar screen renders correctly via ink-testing-library (chip frame assertions for both suspended states). [oracle: bun test test/ui/tab-bar.test.tsx]
userStories.notes: File: test/ui/tab-bar.test.tsx (append new test(s); do NOT touch src/ui/TabBar.tsx). Reuse the existing ControlledTabBar wrapper pattern but add a variant that threads the `suspended` prop through to TabBar. Arrow escape sequences: '[C' = Right, '[D' = Left (see existing tests at lines 71/81/95). Use waitForFrame from test/helpers/flush-ink.ts to poll frames, never a fixed setTimeout. For the suspended={true} assertion, after writing arrows, assert the active chip is unchanged (poll a short settle then assert the frame still shows the original active chip); onChange should not fire. TabBar suspends via Ink useInput { isActive: !suspended } (src/ui/TabBar.tsx:46-57). installTerminalSizeMock() is already called at module top. Ink success/failure is the glyph, not divider color: assert on chip bracket text. Curated invariant: no tautological mock-call-only assertions; assert observable frame/onChange behavior.
